newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street stocks extend run into record ground.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street stocks extend run into record ground.

text.p: Stocks moved deeper into record territory Monday, buoyed by a another wave of buying in technology shares.
At 1 p.m. EST, the Dow Jones industrial average was up 8.46 points at 6,841.56 after closing Friday above 6,800 for the first time at a record 6,833.10.
In the broader market, declines led advances by a small margin on moderate volume of 247 million shares.
The Nasdaq composite index, which is laced with technology stocks, rose 12.81 points at 1,361.86, surpassing Friday's record finish of 1,349.05.

Analysts said the Nasdaq's rally was fuelled good earnings from Microsoft Corp., which reported after Friday's close that it had earned $741 million in the latest quarter, compared with $575 million a year earlier.
"We are having a Nasdaq day," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd.
"The Microsoft numbers were strong. There is a follow through of upward momentum on Nasdaq, and it has been outperforming the other averages all day," he said.

Microsoft, the most actively traded Nasdaq issue, was up 2-7/8 at 90. Other high techs followed, with Intel up 1-13/16 at 145-7/8, Cisco Systems Inc. 2-1/16 higher at 74-11/16, U.S. Robotics Corp. up 2-1/4 at 73-7/8 and Ascend Communications Inc. up 1-7/8 at 76-7/8.
Microsoft warned about slower earnings growth in 1998, but the market took it in stride. "They always issue a warning but remain the undisputed software champ," Bleier said.
The bond market was closed in observance of Martin Luther King Jr Day.

Elsewhere in the stock market, First USA Inc. rallied 8-5/8 to 45-3/8 on its agreement to be acquired by Banc One Corp. for stock worth $6.6 billion at Monday's prices. Banc One was down 3-3/4 at 41-3/8.
Shares of other credit card issuers rose in sympathy with the news, with Advanta Corp. up 4-3/8 at 47-1/2. MBNA Corp. gained 1-3/4 at 32-7/8 and Capital One Financial Corp. rose 4-1/4 to 37-3/4.
But Hugh Johnson, chief investment officer at First Albany Corp., said that while the sector would benefit, the merger had little effect on the overall market.
"What helps stocks, in my view, is when one company buys another for cash. That means there is a flow of money into the stock market," he said.
"In this case Banc One is buying First USA for stock so that while it is a big and interesting deal, it does not in my mind improve where the overall stock market is heading," he said.
